drafted_from: tool:save-a-form's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep a form, a list of questions people answer, as one of the person's own records so it can be asked and its answers checked", with {"form_id":"sample-intake","title":"Sample intake","questions":[{"questionId":"budget","questionTypeId":"number","label":"Budget"}]}. It runs tool:save-a-form and answers {"saved":true,"form_id":"sample-intake","record_id":"question-sequence:sample-intake","question_count":1}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (question-sequence) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Keep a form, a list of questions people answer, as one of the person's own records so it can be asked and its answers checked", and give it form_id (The form's name, kept in the record id); questions (The questions, in order).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:save-a-form and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: Give a form_id, an optional title and presentation, and the questions.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: question-sequence (records:write).
